### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e07566b737f80115aa962ae78eac3aa5f103babb`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e07566b737f80115aa962ae78eac3aa5f103babb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fce87598cb37e5f1fd6e49c3d71830390134ee36` — the merge of head `d076cc606a94380806a1e4299737f10f44f6fb17` into base `e07566b737f80115aa962ae78eac3aa5f103babb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fce87598cb37e5f1fd6e49c3d71830390134ee36 && git checkout fce87598cb37e5f1fd6e49c3d71830390134ee36
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e07566b737f80115aa962ae78eac3aa5f103babb d076cc606a94380806a1e4299737f10f44f6fb17 && git checkout -B drift-repro e07566b737f80115aa962ae78eac3aa5f103babb && git merge --no-ff d076cc606a94380806a1e4299737f10f44f6fb17

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e07566b737f80115aa962ae78eac3aa5f103babb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e07566b737f80115aa962ae78eac3aa5f103babb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d076cc606a94380806a1e4299737f10f44f6fb17`
Local-runs: none

Record written 2026-10-01T06:54Z by an isolated reviewer for the `domain:services` seat (#6021). Inputs: card #21062 (body and all six comments), PR #21101 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at the merge-base `63d1a7c378`), and the head's check-runs. Read-only: nothing built, run or re-run; the diff was read from `git fetch origin pull/21101/head` and `git show` of the base and head blobs. Disclosure: classes and positions only, as the family's discipline requires.

### ① Derived judgments

Four files, +537 / −25: the plugin source, a plugin pin, a dogfood pin and the changeset. Each judgment names the position it was read at (line numbers are the head's unless marked base).

1. **One masker, byte-identical extraction — RIGHT.** Step 4's body (base `security-plugin.ts` :3838–:3860, 23 lines) and the body of the new private `maskOperationResult` (head :9048–:9070) are identical after a two-space dedent: same md5, empty diff. Step 4 still calls it at the same position — the last statement of the middleware callback, after the post-write seam check (head :3886) — with the same three resolved inputs plus the delegator list it already held. No non-grant caller's behaviour moves. The method sits beside `computeReadPartialMaskRules`, as declared.
2. **Admission unchanged — RIGHT.** The admission predicate (the declared object only; the create and the three read-back operations) and the server-managed field strip lie between the two grant hunks (base :2018 and :2055) and are not in the diff; the refusal for any other operation or object is the same statement as before. The grant branch's only behavioural edits are the block that replaces `return next()`.
3. **The grant resolves its caller as the data plane does — RIGHT, on both deployment shapes.** Same primitives, same order, same position (before `next()`): `resolvePermissionSetsForContext` on the grant's context, with the data plane's fail-closed catch (head :2077 mirrors :2218 — same error class, same code, same log shape), then `resolveCallerPosture` on those sets, with the data plane's unresolved-posture refusal (head :2090 mirrors :2322 — same wording helpers, same error class). The delegator is `null`: the data plane resolves one only when sets resolved and the context carries a delegation link, and the route-built grant context carries neither a principal nor a link (head `rest-server.ts` :10826), so the two agree on every door in the tree. No guest set registered: the named set resolves to nothing, no user id means no baseline and no post-resolution fallback (head :6348), zero sets, and `resolveCallerPosture` answers the stand-in — the object's masking rules, no capability fold. A guest set registered: that set, and the object's posture as it is. Each shape's premise is pinned first in the unit file, so a later change to resolution moves the pin loudly.
4. **The principal-less hand-off is unreachable through the grant — RIGHT.** The grant branch (head :2032) precedes the hand-off (head :2206), and every path under a grant context that names an object either returns after masking or throws. A grant context carrying no position, no named set and no user id still resolves zero sets and is masked by the stand-in (pinned). This is stricter than the data plane's own hand-off for the same shape, which is the direction triage ruled: the grant never bypasses the masker.
5. **Two fail-closed refusals — RIGHT, and not reachable on a healthy door.** Both are the data plane's existing refusals (#3545 and the resolution-failure deny) applied to the one branch that skipped them; both throw before `next()`, so nothing is written behind either. Reachability: the resolution refusal needs a degraded metadata or db loader; the posture refusal is set only when the object's declaration cannot be read (head :8773), and on the submit door the object is the form's declared target, which the create itself requires — so neither fires in a healthy composition. Pinned at the unit layer (a throwing resolver; an empty schema registry). The grant used to be the one door that would let an echo out past an unreadable posture; it now refuses as every other caller is refused.
6. **Public surface changed: the anonymous public-form submit door's `201` echo — a narrowing, RIGHT.** On both shapes a field whose masking rule applies is echoed masked, the one filled from its default included; on a guest-set deployment a field that set marks unreadable, or whose capability contract it does not hold, is dropped from the echo — exactly the data plane's answer for that caller. No new key on any payload. The grant-admitted read-back operations are masked by the same call; no door issues them under the grant — the only construction site of a grant context in the tree is the submit route, and it issues one create (head `rest-server.ts` :10826–:10840).
7. **Type surface — RIGHT.** The addition is a private method on the plugin class; plugin-security has no API report and the repo's api-surface gate is spec-scoped. No export, type or spec key moves.
8. **The stand-in's region is untouched — RIGHT.** The four source hunks (base :2018, :2055, :3834, :9001) all lie outside both stand-in regions. Verified by blob: base :5600–:5760 vs head :5624–:5784 (the `resolveCallerPosture` docblock and body) and base :2230–:2250 vs head :2274–:2294 (its call site) are byte-identical. #21063's edit therefore merges textually clean, and because the grant branch now reads the posture through the same call, that edit reaches this door with no further change.
9. **Pins — RIGHT by class.** Unit: both shapes, premise first; masked echo on the create and on the admitted read-backs; the no-rule control stored; admission unchanged (create runs, strip holds, other operation and other object refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` before running); the principal-less grant masked; the two refusals before the operation runs. Dogfood: a real boot per shape over the anonymous door, with a system read proving the stored values. Fixture spellings in both files are synthetic, not readings. Red-then-green and the ablation (predicted five masker pins and both dogfood pins, observed exactly those) are the dev's measurements, read not re-run.
10. **`main` movement — RIGHT.** The head is a merge of the fix onto `main` at the merge-base; `main` has since moved 9 commits (the report said 8 at its reading), none touching any of the four files. The queue rebuilds on them.
11. **Hygiene.** No model identifier anywhere in the diff. The PR body, the dev report and the seat's ACCEPT comment stay by class.

**Gate verdicts (the head's check-runs, read after the last one completed):** 35 check-runs on `d076cc606a`, all completed — 32 success, 3 skipped, 0 failure. The three skips are the docs build, the console pin gate and the opt-in packed-tarball smoke: path-scheduled or opt-in, none owed by this diff. Green by name: Check Changeset (which executes `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major` against the merge-base), Lint & Repo Gates, Type Check source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger / workspace and TypeScript Type Check, Test Core 1–6, Dogfood Regression Gate 1–3, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Build Core, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, the claim guards (same issue, same single-writer path, Part-of not closing its card, the card claims this branch), Check PR Size, Auto Label, and the two docs checks. Every check green, which the Tier S landing also requires.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/21062-public-form-read-back-masking.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-security: minor`, summary line with the conventional `!`, a `**BREAKING` banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in the body, and `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The PR's line 2 carries the same `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; the claim expected that spelling.

Judged against the diff:
- **`no`** is true: the diff adds no key to any published payload and widens no accept set.
- **`(narrowing)`** is true: a public caller's echo now carries masked values and, on a guest-set deployment, fewer keys; a client that read a stored value back out of the submit response breaks. That is the arm's purpose (#16421), and it carries the breaking signal the gate reads.
- **`minor`, not `major`, not `patch`:** the launch-window guard pushes a breaking changeset to `minor`; a breaking narrowing is not a `patch`. The one package bumped is the one whose published source moves; the dogfood package is private.
- **Not `skip-changeset`:** a released package's behaviour moves.
- **ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`:** honest. Nothing an author wrote is removed, renamed or re-meant — every masking rule already declared itself for this caller class — so no mapping is owed, and the body carries none (its closing paragraph is a consumer note, not a rewrite prescription). The `Check Changeset` run, which executes both `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major` on this PR, concluded success on the head.

`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — RIGHT. Level `minor` with the breaking carriers — RIGHT.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`:** none filed. Nothing to answer.
- **Dev deviation 1 (no empty-branch push before the first edit):** process only; no bearing on the diff. Noted.
- **Dev deviation 2 (two new refusals on failure paths):** judged at ①.5 — right, pinned, stated in the changeset's own paragraph.
- **Dev deviation 3 (`main` merged once, then moved on):** judged at ①.10 — none of the later commits touches this diff.
- **Dev deviation 4 (long lock hold):** process only; no bearing on the diff.
- **Out-of-scope finding, step 2.9 (the predicate guard does not run under the grant):** no public-door reach — one construction site, one create, no predicate — so by the filing gate it is not a card now. The residual worth naming by position: the grant admits three read-back operations no door issues; a future door that reads under the grant meets this guard first. Noted on this record; no card.
- **Out-of-scope finding, step 2.5a (the masked-echo write refusal does not run under the grant):** value integrity on an anonymous create, not exposure; unchanged by this diff. No card.
- **Out-of-scope finding, the capability class on a no-guest-set deployment:** this one DOES have public-door reach today — a capability-gated field with no masking rule, filled from its default, is still echoed stored to an anonymous submitter where no guest set is registered. It is a data-exposure class, and it is carried: #21063 (`domain:spec` seat 2, claimed, same file, the stand-in's region) adds the capability fold the stand-in lacks, and ①.8 shows that fix reaches this door through the shared call with no further edit here. No new card; the carrier is the right one. Escalation: none, beyond noting that #21063's landing is what closes the class on this door.
- **The seat's surface amendment (step-4 extraction outside the claimed region, same file), declared to the `domain:spec` seat:** judged at ①.1 and ①.8 — it is the only copy-free way to reach the one masker, and it does not touch the stand-in's region. The declaration was the right act.
- **Disclosure:** the PR body, the dev report and the ACCEPT comment state everything by class; readings stay private. This record does the same.
